Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-02
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lina Park (Redwood CSM), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Dana Alvarez (Orbit Edge - Head of AI Platform), Rohit Menon (Orbit Edge - DevOps Lead), Emily Zhao (Product), Carlos Varela (Security)
Recording id: ff-20251202-orbitedge-001

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
We walked through the proposed 4-week onboarding sprint for Orbit Edge's Redwood deployment: staged environment, SSO/SAML, VPC peering/staging, data handling/KMS, and pilot success criteria. Action items assigned for staging account, security docs, and technical deep dive. Customer raised questions about private deployment options and rollout timelines; security needs around KMS and audit logs were emphasized.

Topics:
- Sprint cadence and owner responsibilities
- Staging environment and VPC/egress/IP allowlist
- SSO/SAML + RBAC mapping
- Data residency, KMS/HSM options, and retention
- Pilot success criteria and evaluation metrics
- Next steps and scheduling a technical deep dive

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina Park: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. We're going to run about an hour, maybe a touch over, we're going to walk through the sprint plan for Orbit Edge onboarding and make sure owners and dates are clear. Uh Marcus and I will handle the engineering bits and Lina will run the playbook. Sorry, I mean I will run the playbook — Marcus? (laughs)
[00:23] Marcus Chen: Yeah hi all, Marcus here. Quick intro from me — I'll own the staging infra and the demo pipelines. I'll also set up the example Terraform bits for your infra team.
[00:35] Dana Alvarez: Thanks. For context, our goal is to have a pilot with 5 production-ish endpoints by end of January, with SLA-ish targets in place. We want to validate latency and cost tradeoffs since we do customer-facing features.
[00:50] Rohit Menon: And security is a big check for us — KMS integration, SSO, audit logs, who can see embedding data, data retention rules.
[01:05] Emily Zhao: From product side we want to evaluate offline quality metrics and some AB tests vs our current baseline model.
[01:12] Carlos Varela: Also SOC2 evidence and if possible a network path diagram for the private deployment.
[01:20] Marcus Chen: Great. High level sprint: week 0 — environment provisioning, week 1 — SSO + RBAC mapping, week 2 — data ingest and KMS tests, week 3 — pilot run and metrics collection, week 4 — wrap + knowledge transfer. We recommended a four-week sprint but can compress if you have strong infra resources.
[01:45] Dana Alvarez: Four weeks sounds right. One question: we need to understand Dedicated capacity vs Redwood Private — what's the operational difference? We want to keep throughput predictable but also minimize data exfil risk.
[01:58] Marcus Chen: Sure. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in Redwood's hosted environment, good for throughput predictability and simpler networking. Redwood Private is the VPC/on-prem option — control plane is customer-managed and network is fully isolated, often used for regulated workloads. There's a small tradeoff: Private requires a bit more setup time and an infra handoff but gives the strongest data residency guarantees.
[02:22] Dana Alvarez: Ok, and latency differences? Roughly similar if we colocate? We care about p95 token latencies.
[02:30] Marcus Chen: Right — if we pin hardware and region you can match latency. We should run a short benchmark once staging is up — Marcus: we'll set up a mini-benchmark to measure p50/p95.
[02:44] Marcus Chen: Note: our KV cache behavior and batching settings can move cost vs latency points a lot — we'll propose default profiles and then tune per endpoint.
[02:55] Rohit Menon: For network we need to know what IPs to allow. We'll do an allowlist on our side. Is there a static range for Redwood's staging, or do we do peering?
[03:06] Marcus Chen: We can do either. For Dedicated/hosted we provide a set of egress IP ranges; for Private we'd do VPC peering or a transit connection. I'll include the IP ranges in the provisioning note.
[03:18] Carlos Varela: Also, does audit logging capture token-level request traces? We need data access logs and an export path to our SIEM.
[03:28] Lina Park: Yes, we support audit logs and you can stream them to a log sink. We'll share the schema and sample events.
[03:34] (crosstalk)
[03:36] Marcus Chen: Quick note, sometimes our docs show 'Redwood Privatee' (typo) — ignore that, it's the same product — apologies the doc is inconsistent.
[03:44] Dana Alvarez: (laughs) That's fine.
[03:46] Lina Park: Ok moving on, security checklist items: SOC 2 report, encryption-at-rest (KMS), encryption-in-transit, RBAC mapping, SAML identity provider, audit trail, and data retention policies. Carlos — are there any additional compliance items we should add?
[04:05] Carlos Varela: We need the KMS integration details (customer-managed key vs Redwood-managed), and HSM if possible for specific keys. Also need to know retention window options for embeddings and request logs.
[04:17] Marcus Chen: We support both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed keys; we'll document the KMS flow and a sample KMS policy. HSM-backed keys are available in Private deployments — we'll scope that in the tech deep dive.
[04:31] Emily Zhao: For success criteria, we'll measure latency, token cost per 1k responses, and an offline quality delta on our validation data. Should be a simple spreadsheet.
[04:43] Dana Alvarez: Yes, send a template for the success metrics.
[04:46] Lina Park: We'll attach one to the sprint plan. On tooling, we'll give you a sample prompt set and evaluation harness. Marcus will also add an embeddings rerank example.
[04:58] Rohit Menon: About data flow: when we push data to Redwood for embeddings, is it stored long term? We need a TTL and assurances about deletion.
[05:07] Marcus Chen: By default we persist embeddings for caching and improved reranking, but retention policies can be set per project. For regulated datasets we can set a short retention or opt out. We'll include a deletion flow and API for purge.
[05:19] Dana Alvarez: Good. Also, are there plug-and-play SDKs we should use for Java/Go? Our stack is mostly Go and Python.
[05:27] Marcus Chen: We have official SDKs for Python/Go and a REST API; I'll attach sample clients. The Terraform provider for infra is also available.

[05:40] — Mid call discussion: Marcus screenshares infra diagram (note in transcript: artifact link)
[06:05] Marcus Chen: Sharing the quick start repo link: https://redwood.app/s/oe-onboarding-quickstart (placeholder)
[06:12] Dana Alvarez: We got it, thanks.

[06:20] (40 minutes of detailed infra & policy discussion omitted here for brevity in notes but captured in recording)

[46:30] Marcus Chen: Back to scheduling — we propose a technical deep dive next Tuesday, 2025-12-09, 14:00 UTC, to demo the KV cache behavior and to run the p95 latency probe. Does that work?
[46:44] Dana Alvarez: That works for us.
[46:46] Emily Zhao: We'll invite our ML engineer to the deep dive as well.

[47:00] Lina Park: Quick recap of owners and dates (recap is somewhat auto-generated in notes):
- Lina: Share sprint plan doc + onboarding deck and calendar invites — due Friday 2025-12-04.
- Marcus: Provision staging account, example Terraform snippets, and sample benchmark scripts — due Sunday 2025-12-06.
- Orbit Edge (Rohit/Dana): Provide IP allowlist, VPC CIDR, list of users to invite to staging, and pilot dataset access — due 2025-12-05.
- Orbit Edge (Dana): Finalize success criteria and provide evaluation dataset — due 2025-12-08.

[47:45] Carlos Varela: One more security ask: can you send a network diagram and an expected data flow for Private vs Dedicated? We need that for our auditors.
[47:55] Lina Park: Yes, Marcus will add network diagrams to the security pack we'll send.
[48:01] Marcus Chen: I'll include diagrams and also a short 'how to' for KMS policy snippets.
[48:08] Rohit Menon: On billing — how do we handle pilot costs? Need an estimate for Dedicated vs Private.
[48:16] Lina Park: We'll send a cost estimate and sample usage projections. For Private there is an onboarding fee plus a per-unit compute; Dedicated is usage + reserved commit. I'll have our pricing team attach a draft.
[48:31] Dana Alvarez: Great.

[48:35] (closing)
[48:36] Lina Park: Any other questions before we close?
[48:38] Emily Zhao: None from product.
[48:40] Carlos Varela: No.
[48:42] Dana Alvarez: No, thanks everyone.
[48:44] Lina Park: Thanks all. We'll follow up with notes and the sprint plan. Expect invites and doc links by 2025-12-04.
[48:53] (meeting ends)
